transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hello, Doctor. It's very nice to meet you. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time today. Um, my family actually asked me to come in. They... well, they seem to think I'm doing a bit too much lately. But honestly, I just feel like I finally have the energy to get things done, you know? 

We're moving, and I've been handling all of that, plus I'm rebuilding the new garage—doing it right, the way it should be done. And I've been helping organize things down at the church, too. On top of that, I'm still working... showing the younger guys at the plant how the grinding and blending equipment really ought to be run. It's a lot, I suppose, but I just feel like I'm the only one with the drive to handle it all right now. Does that make sense? I mean, it's not a bad thing to be productive, is it?
Have you ever had a period like this before, or times in the past when your mood or energy was very different from normal—either unusually high like now, or very low and depressed?

Well, um... I don't really think so, Doctor. I mean, I've always prided myself on being a pretty steady guy, you know? I've never really been one to get down in the dumps or... or depressed. I've always tried to just keep a good, positive attitude. I hope that's... I mean, I hope that makes sense. 

And as for the energy, well... maybe I've had good weeks here and there where I get a lot done, but nothing where my wife or the kids ever made a fuss over it before. I just like to stay busy and be useful to people. Does that sound alright to you? I really don't want you to think there's something wrong with my head or anything, I'm just trying my best to be a good provider and help out where I can.

Have you noticed any unusual experiences lately, such as hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or believing you have special powers, abilities, or a mission that others might find hard to believe?

Oh, my. No, no, Doctor, nothing like that at all. I... I certainly don't hear any voices or anything of that sort. And no special powers here, I can assure you. I'm just a regular, hardworking guy. Just trying to do my part, you know? 

I know you probably have to ask everyone these kinds of things, and I don't mind you asking, I really don't. But my mind is as sound as it's ever been. I just have a lot of pep in my step right now, getting the garage up and helping the guys at the plant. I hope... well, I hope that puts your mind at ease? I'd hate for you to think I was losing my grip on reality or something, because I'm really doing just fine. That's a good thing, right?

Has this burst of energy and activity caused any real problems—like conflicts at work, risky decisions, financial issues, or trouble with your family or job—that are clearly different from your usual self?

Well, um... I guess... I guess there have been a few little hiccups, if you want to call them that. But really, nothing I can't smooth over, you know? 

At work, there was a... a bit of a misunderstanding about some safety protocols. I was just trying to show the guys a faster way to run the grinders, but management felt I was rushing things, so they... well, they asked me to take a little time off. Just a temporary thing, I'm sure. It's probably for the best anyway, with the move and all. 

And, um, at home... well, my wife has been a little stressed about the move. She... she actually took the checkbook away, and the car keys. She said I was making too many big decisions too fast with the garage materials and the movers. I think she's just overwhelmed and being a little overcautious, you know how it is. But I let her handle it because I want her to be happy and comfortable. I'm just trying to be a good husband and keep the peace. That's the right thing to do, isn't it? Just let her take the reins for a bit if it makes her feel better?
